competencies.statement: Explain major vehicle-system roles, distinguish observations from diagnostic conclusions, and use safety, professional practice, and technical information to plan an evidence-based next step.
Use observed electrical symptoms and appropriate measurements to plan a vehicle-specific diagnostic check.
Use inspection findings and measurements to diagnose brake-system concerns and verify corrective action.
Interpret operating data and test results to diagnose engine-performance concerns and verify repairs.
Use inspection, geometry, and component evidence to diagnose suspension and steering concerns.
Evaluate complex vehicle-system evidence, uncertainty, competing hypotheses, and verification strategies.
Design and evaluate advanced vehicle-system tests using appropriate instrumentation, controls, and technical evidence.
Design aligned technical curriculum, authentic assessments, rubrics, and feedback systems using measurable outcomes.
Design and evaluate applied technical-education or diagnostic investigations using transparent scholarly evidence.
Use evidence-informed leadership practices to improve technical programs, instruction, learner support, and faculty practice.

Explain electrified-vehicle energy flow, distinguish voltage domains and system roles, and use documented evidence to select safe, vehicle-specific diagnostic next steps without treating one symptom, code, or measurement as proof of component failure.

Recognize automotive shop hazards and professional responsibilities, use applicable safety and environmental information to select a safe next action, and document when work should stop, be controlled, or be escalated.
Apply automotive mathematical relationships with correct units, identify assumptions and required source information, and explain whether a quantitative result is reasonable for the stated problem.
Select an appropriate measurement approach, distinguish a measured value from a specification or conclusion, and document units, instrument context, and source requirements.

Explain foundational automotive electrical relationships, interpret generalized circuit measurements, and justify a safe next diagnostic step while distinguishing project-authored training models from vehicle-specific service information.
Build and evaluate generalized electrical test setups, record measurements with context, and use evidence to justify a safe next diagnostic action.
Explain major engine component and system relationships, distinguish operating evidence from conclusions, and identify when vehicle-specific information is required.

Organize engine laboratory evidence, select appropriate measurement or documentation steps, and recognize when applicable service information is required before a procedure or specification can be used.
Trace generalized drivetrain power flow, identify major subsystem roles, and use observations and applicable information to justify a next inspection or diagnostic question.

Explain generalized HVAC and climate-control relationships, classify operating observations, and identify the applicable information required before interpreting pressures, temperatures, refrigerant handling, or service procedures.
Locate and interpret applicable technical information, distinguish authoritative source content from learner inference, and document the source basis for a diagnostic or service decision.
Analyze advanced engine mechanical relationships, distinguish measured evidence from diagnosis, and identify the applicable service information required before specifications or procedures are used.
Organize engine mechanical laboratory evidence, select an appropriate measurement or inspection approach, and justify a next step using applicable specifications and documented observations.
Collect and interpret generalized engine-performance test evidence, preserve test context and units, and justify a diagnostic next step using applicable technical information.
Explain generalized automatic-transmission power-flow and control relationships, distinguish system evidence from conclusions, and identify applicable information required for diagnosis or service.
Explain electronic signal and control relationships, interpret generalized sensor/actuator evidence, and use applicable technical information to justify a diagnostic next step.
Analyze advanced electrical-system relationships, interpret measurements in operating context, and justify a next diagnostic action using applicable vehicle-specific information.
Organize diagnostic evidence from symptoms, scan data, trouble codes, tests, and applicable information to justify and verify a systematic next diagnostic step.
Plan and document generalized fault-isolation work, collect relevant evidence, and justify a safe next test without substituting assumptions for verified vehicle information.
Explain generalized vehicle-dynamics relationships, apply appropriate quantitative reasoning, and distinguish modeled behavior from vehicle-specific limits or measured evidence.
Explain emissions-system relationships, interpret generalized sensor and system evidence, and identify applicable technical or regulatory information required before diagnostic conclusions are made.
Explain generalized feedback and control relationships, interpret sensor/actuator evidence, and use applicable system information to justify a control-system diagnostic next step.
Integrate multi-domain vehicle evidence, prioritize testable hypotheses, and justify an advanced diagnostic next step using applicable technical information.
Plan and execute generalized advanced diagnostic evidence collection, interpret cross-domain test results, and document a source-supported fault-isolation decision.
Explain generalized vehicle-network relationships, interpret communication evidence, and use applicable architecture and protocol information to justify a network diagnostic next step.
Explain generalized hybrid energy-flow and component relationships, recognize high-voltage safety boundaries, and identify applicable information required before diagnostic or service work.
Organize generalized hybrid laboratory evidence, recognize when work must stop for high-voltage or authorization reasons, and justify an information-supported next diagnostic step.
Organize EV laboratory evidence, recognize high-voltage and charging safety boundaries, and justify a safe next diagnostic action using applicable vehicle and equipment information.
Explain generalized battery and management-system relationships, interpret state and health evidence in context, and identify applicable information required for safe diagnostic decisions.
Explain generalized ADAS sensor and control relationships, interpret system evidence, and identify applicable calibration, environmental, and vehicle information required before service decisions.
Collect and organize generalized vehicle data, evaluate context and quality, select appropriate visual or analytical representations, and justify conclusions without overstating the evidence.

Explain generalized embedded-system and ECU relationships, trace input-processing-output flow, and distinguish conceptual architecture from implementation-specific details requiring authoritative documentation.
Identify generalized automotive cybersecurity assets, threats, and controls, interpret defensive evidence, and document risk and mitigation reasoning within authorized and ethical boundaries.

Explain generalized connected and software-defined vehicle relationships, identify data and software lifecycle dependencies, and distinguish architectural concepts from implementation-specific claims requiring authoritative information.
Formulate an automotive technology research question, organize appropriate evidence and methods, and distinguish source-supported findings from assumptions or unsupported conclusions.
Analyze cross-domain vehicle-system dependencies, identify interface evidence, and justify an integration or diagnostic next step using applicable technical information.

Document supervised professional learning, connect workplace experiences to curriculum competencies, and communicate evidence of growth while respecting organizational safety, confidentiality, and authorization boundaries.

Define an applied automotive technology problem, justify project requirements and methodology with evidence, and produce a traceable project plan with explicit assumptions, constraints, and verification needs.

Execute and document an approved automotive technology project, evaluate test evidence against project requirements, explain limitations, and present conclusions that are traceable to verified results.
Analyze interactions among advanced automotive system domains, identify interface evidence and uncertainty, and design a traceable system-level verification strategy.
Construct and evaluate automotive system models, justify parameter choices and assumptions, and assess model validity against appropriate evidence.
Evaluate vehicle datasets using appropriate analytical methods, distinguish statistical patterns from supported technical conclusions, and document uncertainty and validation needs.
Analyze advanced EV subsystem interactions, evaluate operating evidence across energy-conversion domains, and design a source-supported verification strategy.
Evaluate battery-system models and diagnostic evidence, distinguish estimated states from measured observations, and justify a validation strategy that respects safety and source boundaries.
Analyze vehicle power-electronic energy conversion and control relationships, interpret evidence across electrical and thermal domains, and identify applicable source requirements for validation.
Evaluate vehicle energy-flow strategies, articulate optimization objectives and constraints, and justify conclusions using traceable operating evidence.
Analyze advanced vehicle-network behavior and topology evidence, distinguish communication symptoms from root-cause conclusions, and design a traceable network verification strategy.
Evaluate embedded automotive architecture and software/hardware interactions, identify interface evidence and timing constraints conceptually, and design an applicable validation approach.
Evaluate multi-sensor perception evidence, explain sensor-fusion and calibration dependencies, and design a validation strategy that documents environment and configuration limitations.
Analyze autonomous-system functional chains, identify cross-domain dependencies and failure evidence, and design a traceable simulation or test validation strategy.
Evaluate automotive cybersecurity risks and controls using threat-model evidence, distinguish defensive verification from exploit development, and document residual risk and validation needs.
Evaluate software-defined vehicle architecture tradeoffs, trace software/data dependencies, and design a configuration-aware verification and lifecycle strategy.
Evaluate advanced automotive control-system models and evidence, assess stability and estimation assumptions, and justify a validation strategy against system requirements.
Evaluate a vehicle digital-twin architecture, distinguish model state from observed vehicle state, and design calibration and validation activities using traceable data.
Critically synthesize current automotive research and technical publications, compare competing claims, and communicate evidence-supported conclusions with explicit uncertainty and source provenance.
